findings.title: Deleting cache does not refresh connected calendars
findings.body: deleteCacheMutation only toasts and calls the optional onSuccess prop. Unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component, it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars (or apps.integrations). SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper owns that query with refetchOnWindowFocus: false and passes props.onChanged, which is often undefined and is not a refetch of this query. After a successful delete the dropdown still shows the old "Last updated" time and "Delete cached data" until a full reload, so the action looks like it failed.

findings.title: Cache timestamp render is not null-safe and ignores locale
findings.body: cacheUpdatedAt is Date | null | undefined, and assigning isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt to hasCache does not narrow it. new Date(cacheUpdatedAt) is therefore a strict-null type error, and if a null/invalid value is formatted, Intl.DateTimeFormat.format throws RangeError and crashes the whole connected-calendars list. The formatter is also hardcoded to "en-US", so every locale sees US date/time formatting inside an otherwise translated string.

findings.title: updatedAt backfill marks every existing cache as just written
findings.body: ADD COLUMN updatedAt TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW() sets every existing CalendarCache row to the migration transaction time. The new UI treats that value as "Last updated", so on deploy every Google calendar with a cache row looks freshly synced even if the row is old or already past expiresAt. now() is STABLE, not a constant, so Postgres cannot use the PG11 fast-default path and will rewrite CalendarCache under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock. The header comment also says the column was added without a default, which is the opposite of this SQL. Backfill from a real write time (or leave the column nullable until the next upsert) and avoid a single volatile default on a large table.

findings.title: Every cache fill rewrites all SelectedCalendar rows
findings.body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache now calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) after writing CalendarCache. That runs on the Google webhook/cache-refresh path and updates every SelectedCalendar for the credential even though the selection did not change. The new UI never reads SelectedCalendar.updatedAt; it reads CalendarCache.updatedAt, which Prisma already bumps on calendarCache.upsert. The empty data object does not set updatedAt explicitly (it only works if Prisma injects @updatedAt), and updateManyByCredentialId types data as SelectedCalendarUpdateInput, which is not updateMany's UpdateManyMutationInput, so this can fail typecheck or throw at runtime after the cache write already succeeded. Remove the call.

findings.title: Cache status ignores expiry
findings.body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups CalendarCache by credentialId and takes max(updatedAt) with no expiresAt >= now() filter. getCachedAvailability only serves rows that have not expired, but the settings UI treats any returned updatedAt as an active cache and offers "Delete cached data". Expired rows therefore show a last-updated time and a delete action for data that availability will not use. After the migration backfill, that timestamp is also the deploy time rather than the last real refresh.

findings.title: dev:cron now depends on undeclared npx tsx
findings.body: dev:cron changed from ts-node, which is a devDependency of @calcom/web, to npx tsx. tsx is not declared in this package, and the app is on Yarn 3.4.1, where npx is not the project runner. yarn dev:cron will fail offline, in CI images without npm/npx, or by downloading an arbitrary tsx version outside the lockfile. Add tsx as a devDependency and invoke it via yarn, or keep ts-node.

findings.title: Webhook helper writes the wrong env file and is macOS-only
findings.body: ENV_FILE is ../.env relative to the process cwd, and the script never cds to its own directory. Running bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repo root (the usual way) creates or edits a .env outside the repo and still prints success, so GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL never reaches the app. The update uses sed -i '' (line 68), which is BSD sed syntax and fails on GNU sed, and cleanup always exits 0, including when the tunnel URL cannot be parsed or sed fails. Resolve the env path from the script location, use a portable in-place edit, and exit non-zero on failure.

findings.title: Empty actions slot still reserves width
findings.body: DisconnectIntegration used to be omitted entirely for delegation credentials and when connection changes are disabled. It is now always wrapped in a flex w-32 div, while CredentialActionsDropdown returns null when the user cannot disconnect and there is no cache. Those rows keep an empty 8rem actions column, shifting the calendar card and error alert layout.

findings.title: No tests for cache delete authorization or status mapping
findings.body: deleteCache is a new authenticated mutation that deletes CalendarCache rows after a userId ownership check, and connectedCalendars now exposes cacheUpdatedAt from getCacheStatusByCredentialIds. There are no tests for a missing/foreign credential, a successful delete, the plain Error (which tRPC surfaces as 500 rather than NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN), or for expired vs active cache rows. A regression in the where clause would let one user wipe another user's availability cache or leave the settings UI stale.
